Our first man home was Dick Tobin who had been troubled by cramp in the Upminster race and then followed Bert Smith and Syd Ring who came in together.

The others followed at short intervals, Charlton 20th, Tobin 38th, Heard and Ken Stimpson 50th, MacDonald 60th and Housego 130th. The next time we saw them, which was about 5 miles, Ferguson had opened up a gap between Field and Thompson; our runners were round about the same as before.
Positions of our men were—4, Tobin; 5, McDonald; 8, Stimpson; 10, Whitehead; 14, Penstone. In the Mitcham A.C. 15 miles open road race we had quite a good number of our members competing and B.

Going back that far reminds me of that exceptional performance in 1945 when with Burfitt (1), Main (2), Pearson (3) and Eeles (13) Belgrave 'A' won with 19 points, to be followed by Tobin (5), Clinton (7), Smart (17) and Jarlett (26) who brought home Belgrave 'B' in second place.

1938 was a quiet year for Ted but in the first few days of January 1939 he finished second in the Middlesex Cross-country championship, and the Cadogan A.C. team (consisting entirely of Belgrave runners as follows:- Stimpson 2, D. Patience 4, Shields 7, Allum 14, Tobin 15, F.R.
Tobin of Swansea was the winner in 30:14 with Brighton & Hove's P.Bristow 2nd, just 5 seconds ahead of our man. With Stu' Paton 8th in 31:11 and Jon Hobbs 12th in 31:45 the Bels took 4th team place.
